title: Backport CUTLASS compatibility shim + Triton plugin ABI preflight checks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Upgrading our runtime to support newer Triton/CUDA toolchains exposed brittle assumptions about CUTLASS minor versions and Triton plugin ABIs. Several customers hit failures when nodes in a Dedicated pool had mixed CUTLASS runtimes or when a Triton plugin changed its exported symbol layout. These failures show up as opaque load-time crashes or silent perf regressions.

Goal: Implement a backwards-compatible compatibility shim that allows the runtime to load kernels built against CUTLASS v3 and v4+ within the same runtime (where ABI-compatible), and add a Triton plugin preflight ABI check that fails fast with a guided remediation path. Reduce incident noise and customer impact during rolling upgrades while preserving performance for the common case.

Scope and approach:
- Add a small, well-tested CUTLASS adapter layer (shim) that maps the handful of API/enum changes we rely on so binaries built against v3 can run when v4 is present. The shim lives behind a build flag and is only active when the detected CUTLASS header version mismatches the expected version.
- Introduce a Triton plugin ABI verifier executed at plugin load time that checks symbol versions, expected struct sizes, and a policy fingerprint. If verification fails: log an actionable error, optionally register a graceful fallback to a conservative kernel path, and surface a clear alert in Console.
- Expand CI matrix to include combinations: CUDA {12.2,13.1}, Triton {2.x,3.x}, CUTLASS {3.x,4.x}, and the two compiler toolchains we ship (GCC 12, Clang 15). Use a fast smoke layer for PRs and a daily expanded matrix for release branches.
- Performance cleanup: where the shim routes to alternative kernel implementations, add a lightweight autotune step (runtime heuristic) to pick block sizes for small sequence lengths to avoid regressions. Remove an old deprecated non-quantized kernel path that regressed GEMM occupancy.
- Tests: unit coverage for shim translation logic, integration job that builds kernels under both CUTLASS versions and runs end-to-end generation for seq-len profiles (16, 128, 1024). Add deterministic microbench harnesses to CI artifacts for perf tracking.

Success criteria:
- No new Dedicated/Private pool incidents related to CUTLASS/Triton ABI after rollout (two weeks post-deploy).
- PRs include green CI on the smoke matrix; nightly expanded matrix shows <= 5% perf delta for common profiles vs. baseline.
- Console surfaces explicit plugin compatibility errors with remediation steps instead of raw crash logs.

Non-goals:
- Full source-level merge between different CUTLASS releases. We target a minimal runtime shim only.
- Major changes to model compiler internals in this ticket (those go into follow-ups).
comments: 2025-02-13 - Aisha: Spike completed. Found 7 symbol/name differences that affect our kernels (mainly enum layouts and a helper API signature). Prototype shim compiles and passes small unit tests on CUDA12+Triton2.

2025-02-20 - Marcelo: Implemented plugin ABI check. It validates a small header struct (magic/version) exported by plugins and rejects unknown versions. Added Console logging with link to docs/helpdesk article.

2025-02-28 - QA (Leah Kim): Integration run against nightly matrix failed on CUDA13+Triton3 for one kernel path (float32 GEMM). Failure traced to an occupancy heuristic—falling back to older launch params restored correctness.

2025-03-02 - Marcelo: Added a lightweight autotune heuristic that measures the first 50 iterations for a new kernel variant and caches optimal block settings keyed by seq_len_bucket. Unit tests added. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4621

2025-03-03 - Design (Ravi): Requested clearer Console UX copy for plugin failures. Updated alert text to include 'recommended action' and 'contact support' with sample command to collect plugin metadata.
2025-03-04 - PM (Sofia): Marking follow-ups for expanding nightly matrix to include our on-prem packaging tests. Also flagged a dependency on ENG-16042 for kernel binding edge cases.

2025-03-05 - Marcelo: Current status — shim merged to runtime/compat branch, ABI verifier behind feature flag, smoke CI green. Nightly expanded matrix still running; two perf regressions (both fixed by autotune). Preparing rollout checklist for staging on 2025-03-12.
Follow-ups: monitor staging telemetry for kernel fallback rate, add telemetry counters (shim_active, abi_check_failures, autotune_success) and a dashboard for the first 48 hours after rollout.
